name: Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
deity: Vishnu as Venkateswara (Balaji, Srinivasa), the lord of the seven hills
period: Ancient foundation; expanded greatly under Vijayanagara
summary: On the seventh of the Tirumala hills stands the most visited and most richly endowed temple on earth, where Vishnu as Venkateswara receives millions of pilgrims a year beneath the gilded Ananda Nilayam tower.

sections.history: The hill shrine of Venkateswara is among the most ancient living temples of the south, with inscriptions attesting royal gifts from the Pallava, Chola and Pandya periods onward. Its golden age came under the Vijayanagara emperors, above all Krishnadevaraya, whose endowments and visits in the sixteenth century made Tirumala the wealthiest pilgrimage centre in India — a status it has never lost. Revered as a Divya Desam and identified with the Kali-yuga form of Vishnu who remains accessible to all who climb the hills, the temple has been administered since 1933 by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams, which today manages one of the largest religious institutions in the world. Generations of devotees have offered their hair, their savings and their vows here, and the unbroken flow of pilgrimage is itself the temple's living history.
sections.architecture: The temple crowns Venkatadri, the seventh peak of the Tirumala range, and is built in the Dravidian manner around a modest but intensely sacred sanctum. Over the garbhagriha rises the Ananda Nilayam vimana, its gilded copper crowning the deity below. Pilgrims pass through successive gateways and halls — the Tirumamani mandapa, the golden entrance — in a tightly managed flow that channels vast crowds toward a few seconds of darshan before the standing image of Venkateswara, dark and richly adorned, one hand pointing to his feet as refuge. Compared with the sprawling temple-cities of the plains, Tirumala's power lies less in monumental scale than in its setting among forested hills and in the sheer density of devotion concentrated on a single doorway.
sections.legends: The sthala purana relates that Vishnu descended to the seven hills as Srinivasa and, to marry the local princess Padmavati, borrowed a vast sum from Kubera, the lord of wealth; devotees' offerings at Tirumala are understood as helping repay that eternal debt, which is why the hundi here overflows. He is Venkateswara, 'the lord who destroys sins', and Balaji to his countless devotees. The custom of tonsure — offering one's hair — is tied to a legend of the goddess and expresses the surrender of ego, while the temple's famous laddu prasadam, prepared in the Potu kitchen, is carried home across the world as a token of the hill lord's grace.
sections.festivals: The nine-day Brahmotsavam in the month of Purattasi (September–October) is the great annual festival, when the processional deity is drawn around the hill in a series of splendid vahanas, culminating in the Garuda Seva that draws the largest crowds of the year. Vaikuntha Ekadashi, Rathasaptami, and the daily sequence of sevas — from the pre-dawn Suprabhatam that wakes the lord to the night's Ekanta Seva — structure a ritual life of extraordinary continuity and detail.
sections.experience: A visit to Tirumala is a pilgrimage in the full sense: many devotees still climb the stone steps of the Alipiri path up the hills, and the darshan itself, however brief, is the culmination of long queues managed through the TTD's token system. Plan ahead, book a darshan slot, and allow time for the whole ritual arc — the hair offering, the laddu, the walk among the shrines. The town of Tirupati at the foot of the hills is the transport base; the hills above are cool, green and, for believers, charged with presence.

visit.timings: Darshan runs from the pre-dawn Suprabhatam through the day into the night, with the sanctum following the TTD seva schedule. Waiting times vary from a couple of hours to many; booked-darshan tokens are strongly advised.
visit.dressCode: Traditional dress is required — men in dhoti/kurta or formal wear, women in saree or salwar-kameez; the temple observes practices for Hindu worshippers and asks pilgrims to declare their faith at entry.
visit.photography: Photography and phones are not permitted inside the temple and are deposited before entry; the sanctum is a strict no-photography zone.
visit.gettingThere: Tirumala sits above Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh; Tirupati has a railway station and airport, and the hills are reached by ghat road or on foot via the Alipiri and Srivari Mettu step paths.
